sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: flashing versus steady signals, arrows versus circles, merge versus added lane, turn versus curve signs, and further warning and intersection signs
Confusable pairs among the markings, signals and warning signs, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, pictures are not described, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A03
A flashing red signal works like a stop sign, while a steady red means stop and wait for green except for a permitted right turn. [A03]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable flashing red versus steady red; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A03
A flashing yellow light means slow and proceed with caution, while a steady yellow means the light is about to turn red and you should stop if you safely can. [A03]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable flashing yellow versus steady yellow; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A04
A green arrow gives a clear path in its direction, while a flashing yellow arrow allows the turn only after you find a gap and yield. [A04]
Why it matters: group arrows; confusable green arrow versus flashing yellow arrow; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A03
A steady red arrow means wait, but a steady yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending and you should get ready to yield or stop. [A03]
Why it matters: group arrows; confusable steady red arrow versus steady yellow arrow; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A05
The Added Lane and Merge signs both warn of traffic entering from another road; the difference is whether the entering traffic gets its own lane or moves into yours. [A05]
Why it matters: group merging; confusable added lane versus merge; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A06
Turn signs and reverse turn signs both point to a top recommended speed of 30 mph or less, while a curve sign only says the advised speed is below the highway's posted limit. [A06]
Why it matters: group curves; confusable turn versus curve sign; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A04
Both white and black are listed as regulatory sign colors, while yellow green is reserved for school signs and yellow for general warnings. [A04]
Why it matters: group sign colors; confusable yellow versus yellow green; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A04
A pennant shape marks a no passing zone, while a pentagon marks a school sign. [A04]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; confusable pennant versus pentagon; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A01
Pavement lines and symbols tell drivers where lanes split, where passing or changing lanes is allowed, which lanes are for turning, where walkers cross, and where to stop. [A01]
Why it matters: group markings; continuation moved from part C; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A01
Marked left-turn lanes use solid yellow lines together with thick yellow stripes on the pavement. [A01]
Why it matters: group markings; confusable with the shared center lane edges.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A02
Never stop in a travel lane, whether you are lost, broken down or dropping someone off; keep going until you can safely pull off. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane rules; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A02
Do not pass using the shoulder, because drivers do not expect a car there and may pull onto it without checking. [A02]
Why it matters: group passing; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A02
Traffic control covers signals, signs and pavement markings, and it can also come from police, highway workers or school crossing guards, whose directions you must follow. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic control; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A02
Crosswalks mark the area where pedestrians are meant to cross the road. [A02]
Why it matters: group crosswalks; glossary crosswalk.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A03
Signals may flash in all directions during emergencies, at night, in periods of light traffic and at special events. [A03]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A05
The School Crossing sign is being changed to a yellow green color over a transition the guide says will take effect within ten years. [A05]
Why it matters: group warning signs; dynamic sign color; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A05
An Exit Speed Advisory sign shows the recommended speed for a highway exit ramp. [A05]
Why it matters: group warning signs; confusable with the curve advisory plate.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A05
A Begin Divided Roadway sign warns that a median or barrier will soon split the two directions of traffic, and End Divided Roadway warns that the split is ending. [A05]
Why it matters: group warning signs; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A06
A large arrow placed on the outside of a turn and chevron signs at curves both stress the need to slow down for a sharp change of direction. [A06]
Why it matters: group curves; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A06
Object markers warn of something in the road or right at its edge, a reminder not to drift out of your lane. [A06]
Why it matters: group special road conditions; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A06
A Bicycle Share the Road sign warns that cyclists may be riding in the same lane as motor traffic. [A06]
Why it matters: group special road conditions; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A07
An Intersection sign warns that another road crosses yours, and a Side Road Ahead sign warns that a road joins from the side the sign shows. [A07]
Why it matters: group intersection signs; confusable crossroad versus side road; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A07
A Roundabout Ahead sign tells you to slow to the posted speed restriction and use the roundabout rules. [A07]
Why it matters: group intersection signs; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A07
A Side Road Railroad Crossing sign warns that tracks cross just beside an intersection, so take care crossing them. [A07]
Why it matters: group intersection signs; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A07
No Trucks and No Bicycles are examples of prohibition signs alongside No Left Turn, No Right Turn and No U-Turn. [A07]
Why it matters: group regulatory signs; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]
